title: Pre-eclampsia
description: This is a serious complication that can affect mum's health and the baby's growth, if not treated early.

contentSections.title: How is pre-eclampsia detected?
contentSections.content: Pre-eclampsia testing typically involves a urine test for mum. One indication of the disorder is an abnormally high level of protein in the urine, which may suggest compromised kidney function.

contentSections.title: What causes pre-eclampsia?
contentSections.content:
Pre-eclampsia develops due to high blood pressure, where blood vessels narrow and limits the blood flow through to vital organs (e.g. brain, kidneys, and liver).

This can lead to the swelling of mum's hands, feet, and face, as well as dizziness, headaches and an increased risk of stroke and cardiovascular diseases later in life. The reduced blood flow may slow down the growth of the baby, and increases the risk of premature birth (<37 weeks) or stillbirth.

contentSections.title: What does this mean for my pregnancy care?
contentSections.content: The condition can be detected and managed through regular, careful checks of mum's blood pressure, blood, urine and baby health throughout the pregnancy. Medication and rest is important for keeping the condition under control.
